findings.title: Resume after Exterminate does not cancel the reaper, so it SIGKILLs the supervisor Nick just resumed
findings.scenario: A live supervisor is 3 minutes into a worker generation. Nick presses Exterminate, then changes his mind and presses Resume within about 10s, before the heartbeat tick has read the flag. Resume clears exterminateRequested and stopRequested (orion-project-agent.mjs:338-340). The next heartbeat tick sees no flag and does not abort (supervisor.mjs:257), so the supervisor carries on. The CLI and Discord both say 'the live supervisor will continue'. At t=20s the detached reaper finds the same pid, start time and boot still holding supervisor.lock and SIGKILLs it mid-task. It never checks that an exterminate is still standing. Result: the task stays `running` with worker.lock held by a dead pid. On Continue it is reconciled to blocked `worker_outcome_unknown`, which spends the attempt and needs Nick. Check subprocesses run in their own process group, so any that were running are orphaned and keep going in the worktree. `serve` sees a non-zero exit and sends the Discord failure alert. If the tick already fired before the resume, the kill controller cannot be un-aborted, so the supervisor exits anyway even though resume reported it would continue.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in a scratch node:test using a temporary HOME, a stand-in process holding supervisor.lock and ORION_EXTERMINATE_GRACE_SECONDS=2. After `exterminate` then `resume`, the output was exterminateRequested=false and stopRequested=false, yet the holder died with SIGKILL, and exterminate.json read {"killed":true,"reason":"pid … did not stop within 2s; killed"}. reap() (lines 80-94) checks only the lease identity: `const same = lease.held && !lease.dead && lease.owner?.pid === pid && …startedAt… && …bootId…`. Neither reap() nor the resume path in steerProjectAgent knows about a pending reaper.
findings.fix: In reap(), re-read state.json before killing and kill only if exterminateRequested is still true and runId matches. Better: store a per-exterminate token in state (for example `exterminateId`), pass it to the reaper, and kill only if that same token is still standing. Resume clears the token, which disarms the reaper. Separately, resume should not say 'the live supervisor will continue' when the supervisor has already tripped its kill controller.

findings.title: A Stop, Pause or Exterminate issued just after Start/Continue is silently cleared by prepareProjectContinuation, and the run proceeds
findings.scenario: Nick presses Continue project, or runs `orion-projects launch <id> 8`, then immediately presses Stop in the panel or sends `agent stop` from Discord. `launch` returns at once and `serve` spends 1-3s in preflight, which runs system_profiler and pmset. On a first start it also spends seconds in `init` (git worktree add), and state.json exists part-way through that. The stop lands and the CLI reports success ('Stop requested'). The panel shows halts while launching (ProjectTab.swift:129). `serve` then calls prepareProjectContinuation, which runs `if (state.stopRequested || state.status === 'paused') state = await steerProjectAgent(project.root, 'resume', …)`. That erases the stop, and the run then works for up to 8-12 hours. An exterminate in the same window is erased the same way, and no reaper is scheduled because no supervisor lease is held yet ('nothing needs killing'). A stop that lands in the later gap, after the continuation but before `orion-agent run` checks for a standing stop, does halt the run. But `run` exits 1, so `serve` records 'failed' and sends the Discord 'could not continue' alert.
findings.evidence: projects.mjs:156 clears any standing stop or pause unconditionally. orion-projects:93 calls prepareProjectContinuation with no record of when the launch was requested. ProjectTab.swift:129 has `if live || launching { return true }`, so halts are offered exactly during this window. orion-agent:204-212 refuses on a stop, and orion-projects:26 rejects on any non-zero exit, which feeds the alert at line 99.
findings.fix: Have `launch` capture the controller revision (or a timestamp) before spawning `serve`, and pass it through. prepareProjectContinuation should clear only halts that were already standing at that revision: do the resume as a transaction with that expected revision, and if a newer halt arrived, abort the launch cleanly with receipt 'stopped' and no alert. Treat a standing stop at `run` start inside `serve` as a clean stop, not a failure.

findings.title: Every reaper hard-kill makes `serve` send a Discord 'project could not continue' failure alert and mark the launch failed
findings.scenario: Nick exterminates, and the supervisor does not release its lease within 20s: it is wedged, still in runtime.probe() loading the model (the heartbeat interval is not armed yet), a slow teardown, or the resume race above. The reaper SIGKILLs `orion-agent run`. `serve`'s child() sees exit code null and rejects. `serve` writes launch.json status 'failed' (the panel shows 'Could not continue') and sends the live Discord alert 'ORION · <name>: the project could not continue. Check its Projects view and run log. No success has been claimed.' The operator's deliberate, successful halt is reported as a run failure on his phone.
findings.evidence: orion-projects:26 has `p.once('exit', code => code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`Agent exited (${code}); see run.log`)))`. Lines 97-99 then run `await receipt('failed',e.message); await sendDiscordAlert(…could not continue…)` for any rejection. orion-project-agent:87 sends SIGKILL, which always produces code null. The docs (§4.20b) describe the kill as the expected exterminate outcome, not a failure.
findings.fix: In `serve`, when the child exits by signal, or with a non-zero code while state.exterminateRequested or stopRequested is set (or exterminate.json shows killed:true for that pid), record receipt 'stopped' ('stopped by operator') and do not send the failure alert.

findings.title: After a hard-killed exterminate, the continued run has runtime recovery switched off for the whole night
findings.scenario: An exterminate is hard-killed by the reaper, or the worker does not settle within settleGraceMs. On Continue, recoverRun reconciles the in-flight task to blocked `worker_outcome_unknown`. That task is not repairable, not retryable and not escalated while other work is claimable (supervisor.mjs:385-393, 408-410, 425-443), so it just sits. But `allowed()` refuses runtime recovery whenever any task carries that blocker. Two hours later Ollama restarts or a reviewer call times out: recoverRuntime returns false, and the supervisor raises a run-level 'repeated_failure' escalation and ends the night (supervisor.mjs:290-297). This is the same failure the 2026-09-23 amendment fixed for parked tasks, reintroduced by one exterminate.
findings.evidence: recovery.mjs:17 has `!state.tasks.some(t => t.blocker === 'worker_outcome_unknown') &&` inside allowed(). reconcileInterruptedRun (orion-project-agent.mjs:496-502) sets exactly that blocker and raises no escalation. ARCHITECTURE 'Reviewer runtime recovery' amendment: 'a parked task switched recovery off … One parked task plus a later Ollama hiccup therefore ended the run.'
findings.fix: Scope the guard to what it protects. Refuse recovery only while worker.lock is held (check() already does this) or while status is 'interrupted', not because a reconciled task keeps the historical blocker. Alternatively, raise a task-level escalation for `worker_outcome_unknown` at reconciliation so the task is parked explicitly and the rest of the run keeps recovery.

findings.title: Continue project is disabled by any open task-level escalation, so a stopped run with a parked task cannot be resumed from the app
findings.scenario: Task T3 is parked by a task-level escalation while T4-T10 remain claimable, which §4.14 says must not stop the run. Nick presses Stop for the evening, or the 8h budget runs out. The next day the Continue project button is disabled because `run?.hasOpenEscalations == true`, even though the controller would happily continue the other tasks. Resume in the panel only clears flags ('no supervisor is running'), and the Discord reply tells him to 'Continue it at the Mac (Projects view…)', which cannot be done. The only paths are resolving T3 first, which requeues it, or the terminal launch command.
findings.evidence: ProjectTab.swift:211 has `.disabled(busy || launching || run?.status == .completed || run?.hasOpenEscalations == true)`. ProjectAgentStatus.swift:159-162 separates isBlocked (status == .escalated) from hasOpenEscalations precisely because a task-level escalation does not halt the run. orion-remote:1095 is the resume reply pointing at the Projects view.
findings.fix: Gate Continue on `run?.isBlocked == true` (status escalated, meaning nothing claimable or a run-level escalation), not on hasOpenEscalations.

findings.title: Halts without a revision still fail with 'state revision changed' when they race a supervisor commit or a second halt
findings.scenario: The panel and Discord deliberately send halts with no revision. The CLI then reads the current revision and passes it as the transaction's expected revision. If the supervisor commits between that read and the state lock (setTaskSubtask, markEscalationNotified, a review result), or if Nick fires Stop from the app and `agent exterminate` from Discord at the same moment, the halt throws 'state revision changed; refresh first'. For exterminate, the reaper is then never scheduled. The failure is reported, but it violates OPERATING §5: 'stopping must never fail because the run moved'.
findings.evidence: Line 123: `const revision = args.length ? Number(args[1]) : (await readProjectAgent(root)).revision;` then steerProjectAgent(root, command, revision). transaction() at orion-project-agent.mjs:274 throws when the revision changed. In a scratch test with a temporary HOME and a background writer committing every 5ms, 7 of 10 consecutive CLI pause/stop calls failed with that message. orion-remote:1127-1131 asserts that 'a halt that can lose a race with the thing it is halting is not a halt'.
findings.fix: For halts given no --revision, run the transaction with `expected = undefined` (steerProjectAgent already validates the command and refuses on a completed run), and keep the revision check only when one was explicitly supplied.

findings.title: Exterminate on a paused run waits out the 15s pause poll, which races the 20s reaper
findings.scenario: The supervisor is paused and sleeping in `await sleep(PAUSE_POLL_MS, signal)`. `signal` is the external SIGINT/SIGTERM controller, not `kill.signal`. Nick exterminates just after a poll began. The heartbeat trips kill within 10s, but the sleep does not wake until 15s. Teardown then runs: resetTree, activity close, releaseAll unloading the still-resident 27B (keep_alive 5m), and the lease release. That can push the release past the reaper's 20s grace (counted from the CLI call), so a supervisor that was exiting cleanly is SIGKILLed partway through its finally. It is left with a dead-owner supervisor lease and, via the finding above, a false 'could not continue' Discord alert.
findings.evidence: supervisor.mjs:357-362: the paused branch sleeps 15s (PAUSE_POLL_MS = 15_000, line 53) on `signal`. kill.abort() at line 259 does not reach this sleep. The reaper grace defaults to 20s at orion-project-agent:128.
findings.fix: Sleep on `AbortSignal.any([kill.signal, signal].filter(Boolean))` in the paused branch, so an exterminate, and ideally a stop via a state re-check, wakes it immediately.

findings.title: Orion can resume Nick's halted run as Nick by forging an inbox envelope that the bridge's next poll processes
findings.scenario: Nick sends `agent pause advance-orion-capabilities` from Discord. The paused supervisor stays alive (supervisor.mjs:356-362). During a later brain turn, or at any other time, Orion runs `orion-remote inject --from <Nick's Discord id> -- agent resume advance-orion-capabilities`. `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` allowlists `~/Desktop/ORION/scripts/orion-remote` with any arguments, and `orion-remote audit` prints Nick's id in its `from` fields. The next Discord message Nick sends within 10 minutes makes the bridge run `orion-remote poll` with `ORION_REMOTE_ALLOW=<Nick's id>`. That poll drains the whole inbox, including the forged envelope. The sender passes the allowlist and `fromPerson()`, the resume clears pauseRequested/stopRequested/exterminateRequested, and the live supervisor carries on. The reply goes only to outbox.jsonl, because the bridge relays only its own envelopeId, and the audit records the resume as Nick's. The same forged path satisfies the sender check on `approve A-XXXX` gate approvals (resolveApproval, line 765).
findings.evidence: `inject` (1433-1450) writes any `--from` straight to inbox.jsonl with no allowlist or provenance check. `poll` (1451-1473) passes `envelope.from` into handle() as the sender. The bridge's dispatch (orion-remote-bridge:206-232) sets ORION_REMOTE_ALLOW to Nick's id and then polls the entire inbox, not just its own envelope. `fromPerson` (1073) only rejects the literal strings "local" and "orion". I reproduced this in a sandbox with HOME set to a temp directory: `inject --from 123456789 -- agent resume demo-proj` run with no allowlist in the env, then `poll` with ORION_REMOTE_ALLOW=123456789, turned a paused state into status ready with pauseRequested false. The audit line read `"from":"123456789","decision":"accepted","verb":"agent","args":["resume",…]`. A direct `handle --from 123456789` from the same env was refused, which shows the only gap is the inbox.
findings.fix: Make the bridge authenticate the envelope it hands over instead of draining a shared queue. The simplest way is for the bridge to call `orion-remote handle --from <author> -- <text>` directly with a fresh envelope id and timestamp, and stop using inject/poll. Otherwise, poll should only process envelopes whose id the caller passes (e.g. `poll --only <envelopeId>`), and inject should refuse any `--from` other than "local" unless it is given a secret that only the bridge holds (for example an HMAC keyed from the installed .env).

findings.title: LOCK ORION disables every Discord agent halt while the dev run keeps running, and the reply says nothing will run
findings.scenario: Nick presses the off switch (`scripts/orion-lock`) before leaving, or it is raised during an incident, while a project run is live. orion-lock does not touch the agentic runtime: it drops the permission profile, disables cron and writes lock.json. The supervisor and worker keep editing and committing. From his phone Nick sends `agent exterminate <id>` (or `agent stop` / `agent status`). handle() checks isLocked() before parsing and returns "Orion is locked. Nothing will run until it is released at the Mac." The halt is never recorded, and the reply tells him the opposite of the truth: the unattended run continues all night.
findings.evidence: orion-remote:1218-1221 rejects every message while lock.json has locked:true, before parse(), so agent verbs get no exemption. A grep of scripts/lib/agentic, orion-agent, orion-projects and lib/orion-project-agent.mjs finds no reader of lock.json or permission-state.json, and orion-lock (stopTheChannel, lines 234-271, plus the profile and cron steps) never halts a project run. I reproduced it in a sandbox: with lock.json {locked:true} and a running project, `handle --from nick -- agent exterminate demo-proj` exited 1 with that sentence and exterminateRequested stayed false. Neither OPERATING.md nor ARCHITECTURE.md mentions this interaction.
findings.fix: Let the halt-direction agent actions (status, pause, stop, exterminate) through the lock after the allowlist check, and keep `resume` blocked. Better still, have orion-lock also record a stop (or exterminate) on the active project run via the operator CLI, and make the locked reply say that the development run is separate if it is not halted.

findings.title: A run-level escalation alert gets exactly one delivery attempt; if it fails, the supervisor exits and nobody is told
findings.scenario: At 01:00 the last claimable task escalates, so state.status becomes escalated. iterate() calls notify(..., force: true) once. The webhook POST fails transiently (a DNS blip, Discord 5xx or a curl timeout), so delivered is false. iterate() then reaches `if (state.status === 'escalated') return true`, the supervisor exits, `orion-agent run` exits 0 and `orion-projects serve` writes receipt 'stopped' without alerting. Nothing retries, so the night's capacity is lost with no alert: the silence failure escalation.mjs was written to prevent.
findings.evidence: supervisor.mjs:333-354: notify is attempted once per pass, and the escalated branch returns true straight after that pass. escalation.mjs:90-91 promises "a failed alert is retried on the next pass rather than forgotten", but for a run-level escalation there is no next pass. orion-projects:96-99 alerts only when the child exits non-zero, and an escalated run exits 0. No other code rereads `notified` after the run exits.
findings.fix: Before returning on an escalated run whose open escalations are still unnotified, retry delivery with a bounded backoff, for example every few minutes up to a cap, keeping the lease and heartbeat. Alternatively, have orion-projects serve send one fallback alert when the run ends escalated with notified:false.

findings.title: Discord halts can still bounce with 'state revision changed; refresh first' although halts are documented as revision-free
findings.scenario: Nick sends `agent exterminate <id>` at the moment the supervisor is committing a stage change. The operator CLI reads state.revision without the state lock. Because the supervisor holds the lock, the CLI's transaction waits (4.20c), then finds revision+1 and throws. Discord relays "could not exterminate: state revision changed; refresh first". That instruction means nothing on a phone, and the halt did not land. Nick has to notice and resend.
findings.evidence: orion-project-agent:123 reads `(await readProjectAgent(root)).revision` outside the lock and passes it to steerProjectAgent. orion-project-agent.mjs:274 then enforces it inside the lock: `if (expected !== undefined && state.revision !== expected) throw new Error('state revision changed; refresh first')`. ARCHITECTURE §4.20b says "None of them needs a revision number… stopping is always safe", and brief.mjs's STOP group says "a halt must never fail because the run moved on". The comment in orion-remote at 1128-1134 calls the race closed, but only the argv revision was removed.
findings.fix: When no --revision is given for pause/stop/exterminate/resume, call the transaction with `expected = undefined` (e.g. let steerProjectAgent accept undefined for halts) so the check happens only when a revision was supplied.

findings.title: Concurrent Discord messages break the replay guard and drop replies (remote-inbound.json is read-modify-written non-atomically by overlapping polls)
findings.scenario: Nick sends two or more DMs in quick succession, for example `agent stop X` then `agent status X`, or a question followed by a command. The bridge handles each MESSAGE_CREATE concurrently and each one spawns its own `poll` over the whole inbox. Overlapping polls read and rewrite remote-inbound.json (`seen`, `hits`, `cursor`) with a plain writeFile, so `seen` updates are lost. The same envelope then executes more than once, which means duplicate brain turns and duplicate mission or approval verbs. A bridge whose own envelope was handled by a sibling poll finds no reply in the outbox and sends nothing, logging "orion-remote declined".
findings.evidence: orion-remote:292 `writeInbound = (next) => writeFile(INBOUND, …)` has no tmp+rename and no lock. handle() does read, check seen, then write at 1238/1264/1276, with no lock around it. orion-remote-bridge:302 runs an unserialized async message handler, and 232 polls the full inbox for every message. In a sandbox stress test (12 simultaneous inject+poll pairs × 5 rounds, `agent status`), 9-11 of 60 messages produced no reply for the dispatching bridge, and each round's audit showed far more than 12 'accepted' entries, so envelopes were executed repeatedly. No envelope was lost outright.
findings.fix: Serialize dispatch in the bridge (a single promise chain), write remote-inbound.json atomically (tmp + rename), and guard handle()'s seen/hits update with the same lock used for remote.json.

findings.title: Escalation alert prints repo-relative commands with no `cd`, so pasting them into a fresh Terminal fails
findings.scenario: The 01:00 alert says `Resolve with: scripts/orion-project-agent --project advance-orion-capabilities resolve --revision N --id … --note "..."` and `N = the "revision" shown by: scripts/orion-agent --project … status`. Nick copies the status line into a new Terminal window, which opens in ~, and gets `zsh: no such file or directory: scripts/orion-agent`. The command reference includes a `cd <repo>` line, but the alert does not, and it is the only instructions he has in hand.
findings.evidence: brief.mjs:52 `cli = (script, projectID) => `scripts/${script}…``, and lines 147-152 build the alert's action lines from it without the `Type these from the ORION folder. First: cd …` intro that commandReference() (line 312) adds.
findings.fix: Include the absolute repo path in the alert's commands (e.g. `~/Desktop/ORION/scripts/orion-agent …`), or add a one-line `cd` to the budgeted action block.

findings.title: When alert delivery keeps failing, every loop pass writes a fresh Astra brief and re-attempts delivery with no rate limit
findings.scenario: A task-level escalation parks one task while other work continues, and the webhook is failing or Discord alerts are switched off in .env. lastAlertAt() stays 0 because recordAlert only runs on delivery, so the 10-minute floor never applies. On every iterate() pass the supervisor runs writeAstraBrief (git log, a diff of up to 60k characters, a 4000-entry journal read, a new file in briefs/) and spawns the alert CLI, which can block for up to 30s when curl hangs. This repeats for every remaining task step all night, filling briefs/ and adding latency to each pass.
findings.evidence: escalation.mjs:99-103: the rate limit is based on lastAlertAt. Line 121 calls recordAlert only when sent.delivered is true. Line 112 writes a new brief for every pending escalation on every call. supervisor.mjs:333-336 calls notify on every pass while any open escalation is unnotified.
findings.fix: Record a lastAttemptAt on every attempt (delivered or not) and rate-limit on that. Write the Astra brief once per escalation id and reuse its path on later attempts.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. Nothing on the resume path disarms the reaper.

1. `exterminate` sets `exterminateRequested` and `stopRequested` (lib/orion-project-agent.mjs:369-370). It then starts a detached `_reap` child. That child gets only the lease owner's pid, startedAt and bootId (scripts/orion-project-agent:96-105).
2. `resume` clears all three request flags without condition (lib/orion-project-agent.mjs:338-340). It has no link to the reaper. No token, no runId and no reaper pid is stored in state.
3. `reap()` (scripts/orion-project-agent:80-94) sleeps for the grace period. It then checks only the lease identity. It never re-reads state.json, so it SIGKILLs a supervisor even after the exterminate was withdrawn.
4. The supervisor's heartbeat tick checks `current.exterminateRequested` (supervisor.mjs:257). If resume lands before that tick, the supervisor carries on as normal and is then killed at 20s. If the tick already fired, `kill` is an AbortController that cannot be un-aborted, so the supervisor exits anyway.
5. In both cases, `resume` prints 'the live supervisor will continue at its next boundary' whenever the heartbeat is live (scripts/orion-project-agent:160-161). That message is false here.

Documented intent: ARCHITECTURE.md (around lines 384-404) says resume continues an exterminated run, and that the reaper kills the process that held the lease 'when exterminate was asked for'. It does not say that a withdrawn exterminate still kills. That harm is not accepted in the docs.

Tests: tests/agentic-halts.test.mjs:48-75 runs resume only after the reaper has already killed the process. No test covers resume inside the grace window.

Severity: I lower this from high to medium. It needs Nick to press Exterminate and then Resume within about 20s. The panel also asks him to confirm Exterminate first. The damage can be recovered: one attempt is spent, the task is reconciled to blocked, and recovery resets the tree. No accepted commit is lost. Still, a control does lie, and a run the operator meant to keep alive is killed.
verdicts.evidence:
- scripts/orion-project-agent:80-94: reap() decides only on `same = lease.held && !lease.dead && lease.owner?.pid === pid && lease.owner?.startedAt === started && lease.owner?.bootId === boot`, then calls process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL'). It never reads state.json.
- scripts/orion-project-agent:96-105: scheduleReaper passes only pid, startedAt, bootId and grace. No exterminate token or runId goes into state or into the reaper.
- scripts/lib/orion-project-agent.mjs:338-340: resume sets pauseRequested, stopRequested and exterminateRequested to false and does nothing about the reaper.
- scripts/lib/agentic/supervisor.mjs:257-259: the heartbeat tick aborts `kill` only if `exterminateRequested` is set. A resume before the tick means the supervisor carries on until the reaper kills it. A tick already fired means abort() cannot be undone.
- scripts/orion-project-agent:160-161: the resume output says 'the live supervisor will continue at its next boundary' whenever the heartbeat is live.
- tests/agentic-halts.test.mjs:66-75: the only exterminate-then-resume test resumes after the SIGKILL, so this path is never tested.
- docs/agentic/ARCHITECTURE.md (around lines 384-404): says 'resume continues it'. It does not say a withdrawn exterminate still kills.

verdicts.reasoning:
I built the scenario step by step and every step holds.

1. The blocker gets set. There are two ways. In the first, the worker does not settle within settleGraceMs after an abort, from either an exterminate or a task timeout (orion-project-agent.mjs:957, 982, 990). That sets blocker 'worker_outcome_unknown' and status 'interrupted'. In the second, the supervisor process is hard-killed while activeTask is set. Either way, the next start calls recoverRun (supervisor.mjs:120-147, also reached from projects.mjs:142-152). recoverRun calls reconcileInterruptedRun (orion-project-agent.mjs:488-507). That leaves the task blocked with 'worker_outcome_unknown', raises no escalation, and moves the status to settleStatus(), which is 'ready' when other work is claimable.

2. Nothing moves the task again. The repair selector excludes this blocker explicitly (supervisor.mjs:385-393). The retry selector only takes 'worker_or_validation_failed' (supervisor.mjs:408-410). The catch-all escalation only fires when nothing is claimable (supervisor.mjs:425-443). No task-level escalation is created, so there is nothing for the operator to resolve either. The historical blocker stays on the task for the rest of the run.

3. Recovery is refused for the whole run. allowed() at recovery.mjs:17 returns false while any task has that blocker. recoverRuntime's first check() throws 'runtime recovery blocked by run controls or unresolved state', the catch returns false (recovery.mjs:104-112), and no budget is claimed.

4. The run ends. In the supervisor catch path (supervisor.mjs:282-297), when there is no stop, pause or exterminate and recovered is false, it escalates run-level 'repeated_failure' and breaks. So one Ollama restart or reviewer timeout, hours later and on unrelated work, ends the night.

The guard is not needed for safety. The danger is a second writer while the first may still be alive, and that is already covered two ways. check() refuses while worker.lock is held (recovery.mjs:48). allowed() refuses status 'interrupted'. Once reconcileInterruptedRun has run, the owner has been proven dead, so the historical blocker protects nothing.

Documented intent does not accept this. The docs say uncertain worker outcomes are "not auto-cleared", which is about recovery never clearing that state. It does not say one should switch recovery off for everything else. OPERATING.md:444 describes the blocker as reconciled on the next start with the attempt spent deliberately. The 2026-09-23 amendment (ARCHITECTURE.md:670) calls a stuck task disabling recovery a defect ("One parked task plus a later Ollama hiccup therefore ended the run"). This is the same failure with a different kind of stuck task.

Why medium and not higher: the outcome is a loud stop with a run-level alert, not silent loss. No work or state is lost. It needs an uncommon starting point (an unsettled worker after abort, or a hard kill mid-task) plus a later transient failure. The alert's reason, 'runtime recovery could not resume', is also slightly misleading: recovery was refused before it was attempted.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. I looked for a guard on the app side, the launch side and in the docs, and found none that would allow a Continue, or that documents this block as intended.

- **App side.** ProjectTab.swift:211 disables the Continue project button whenever `run?.hasOpenEscalations == true`. ProjectAgentStatus.swift:261 (`canResume`) also needs `!run.hasOpenEscalations`. So with one task parked, the panel's Resume is disabled as well as Continue. Nothing in the panel lets Nick restart the other tasks without first resolving the parked one.
- **Backend side.** No backend guard needs this block. In scripts/orion-projects:50-96, `launch`/`serve` refuse only for a held live lock, disabled execution, or a completed plan. `prepareProjectContinuation` (projects.mjs:139-158) only reconciles and clears stop/pause. The supervisor treats task-level escalations as non-halting: supervisor.mjs:348-352 stops only on `status==='escalated'`, and :410 filters out only the parked task. So the terminal launch would carry on with T4-T10, and only the app refuses.
- **Documented intent points the other way.** ARCHITECTURE §4.14 says a task escalation "parks that task alone, and the loop carries on". It also says the UI must tell "something needs you" apart from "the run stopped". The Swift header comment (ProjectAgentStatus.swift:17-21) warns that conflating `hasOpenEscalations` with `isBlocked` is wrong. OPERATING.md:47 says `launch` is the "Same as Start / Continue in the Projects tab", and :430 says "a task-level escalation parks one task and the night continues". ARCHITECTURE:670 records a sibling bug that was already fixed: a parked task turned off recovery. This gate is the same conflation.
- **Discord reply.** The reply at orion-remote:1095 sends Nick to the Projects view, which will not work in this state. The same sentence also gives the working CLI command.

**Why medium:**
- It does not lose work, and nothing runs when it must not.
- Workarounds exist: resolve the parked escalation first (which forces a decision Nick may not want to make yet), or use the terminal launch command.
- The operator's main control is disabled for no reason the docs accept. The status line shows "Needs attention" rather than showing that the plan could continue. A real morning-after or post-budget continue from the app stalls.

**Fix:** gate Continue on `isBlocked`, or on nothing escalation-related, since a run-level escalation already makes `status` escalated. The same gate in `canResume` needs looking at too.
